guidance.overview: Technical objections arise when the customer doubts the solution can meet a specific requirement. Acknowledge the concern, use only verified product facts, and flag anything that needs specialist validation.
clarify_first: Can you tell me more about the specific requirement or workload you are concerned about?
Is this based on something you have seen in a previous evaluation, or a current requirement you need to meet?
What does the technical team need to see to feel confident?
guidance.acknowledge: Technical fit is critical — it is the right thing to validate carefully before making any commitments.

response_points.detail: Reference only what the product knowledge tool has returned with a source. Do not add capabilities from memory.
response_points.label: Verified — cite source_id from tool result

response_points.detail: State any limitations returned by the product tool. Customers trust sellers who acknowledge constraints.
response_points.label: Verified — from product limitations field

response_points.detail: For anything the product data does not confirm, propose a technical proof of concept, architecture review, or specialist call rather than asserting fit.
response_points.label: Standard guidance — no product claim

guidance.reframe: Position any gap as a question to investigate together: 'That is an important requirement — let me connect you with the technical team who can validate it properly.'
guidance.propose_next_step: Offer a technical deep-dive session or architecture workshop with a specialist.
do_not_say: Capability claims not supported by a tool result.
Performance figures, benchmark results, or certification claims not in the product data.
Compatibility or integration claims without a verified source.
